items.promptRaw:
Please use "Pop-in" (ポップイン), one of the names in "Motion graphics moves".
Motion Prompt #001

What it is: Pops into view with a small bounce
What the sample shows: An app icon pops in with a bounce, then a notification badge pops in a moment later.
Spec:
- One pop per 2.35 s (twice per 4.7 s cycle: a star on coral first, then a heart on blue).
- Icon: 116 px rounded square (radius 30). From 0.28 s, scale 0→1 with a spring: 1 − e^(−6.5t)·cos(15t), peaking at about 1.26.
- At the same time, rotation −0.35 rad (about −20°) → 0 with a spring: 1 − e^(−6t)·cos(11t).
- Badge: yellow circle, radius 25, with "1", at the icon's top-right (+52, −52). Starts at 0.62 s with spring 1 − e^(−7t)·cos(17t).
- Exit: 1.86–2.12 s. Scale is multiplied by (1 − backIn, s = 2.2), so it swells slightly and then shrinks to 0.
- Floor shadow: 62 × 8 ellipse that scales with the icon (clamped to 0–1).
When to use it: Use it to bring in a small element such as an icon, button or badge with a light accent.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/001.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/motion.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Burst" (バースト), one of the names in "Motion graphics moves".
Motion Prompt #003

What it is: Lines and dots burst outward as something appears
What the sample shows: A like heart fills in, and a ring, lines and dots burst outward at the same moment.
Spec:
- One burst per 2.35 s. A heart (size 46, 7 px outline) sits in the centre.
- Anticipation: 0.3–0.5 s, scale 1→0.7 (quadratic ease-in-out).
- Trigger at 0.5 s: the heart fills with coral and scale returns 0.7→1 with spring 1 − e^(−6.5t)·cos(16t).
- Ring: yellow, radius 44→90 while line width goes 16→0, over 0.6 s with quintic ease-out.
- 10 radial lines (yellow/mint alternating, width 9): outer end radius 64→130 (y scaled 0.82); length 36 shrinks to 0 between 0.22 and 0.7 s after the trigger.
- 10 dots (coral/blue alternating, radius 8→4.8): radius 58→150 on an ellipse (x ×1.45, y ×0.78), fading out 0.3–0.72 s after the trigger. The heart fill fades at 1.92–2.2 s.
When to use it: Use it to mark the instant something is triggered or achieved, such as a like, a success or a correct answer.

Please use "Line draw" (ラインドロー), one of the names in "Motion graphics moves".
Motion Prompt #004

What it is: A line extends as if it were being drawn
What the sample shows: A chart line draws itself on, and is later erased from its starting end.
Spec:
- One pass per 4.7 s. Drawn as a trim path: animate the visible range (start fraction to end fraction) of each stroke.
- Axes (L shape, width 6) draw at 0.08–0.7 s; the line (mint, width 11, a smooth curve through 7 points, round caps) draws at 0.4–1.95 s. Both use cubic ease-in-out.
- While drawing, a yellow dot (radius 12, white centre radius 5) rides the leading tip.
- Arrowhead: opens at 1.9–2.2 s with backOut (s = 2.5); wings 26 long, 20 wide.
- A coral circle (radius 26, width 7) is drawn around one peak at 2.2–2.8 s, clockwise from the top.
- Erase: circle 3.5–4.0 s, line 3.65–4.45 s, axes 3.85–4.55 s, each shrinking from its starting end. The arrowhead fades at 4.3–4.45 s.
When to use it: Use it when the stroke itself is the point: charts, routes, underlines, hand-drawn circles.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Typewriter" (タイプライター), one of the names in "Motion graphics moves".
Motion Prompt #006

What it is: Text appears one character at a time, as if typed
What the sample shows: Text is typed into an input field one character at a time, then the send button lights up and is pressed.
Spec:
- One pass per 4.7 s. Nine characters appear in a white input field (471 × 92, radius 30), one every 0.24 s starting at 0.3 s (typing ends at 2.46 s).
- Each new character settles from scale 1.35 to 1: 1 + 0.35·e^(−16t).
- Cursor (coral, 5 × 44) sits after the last character: solid while typing, otherwise blinking with a 0.94 s period (on for 0.5 s).
- Send button (radius 30): grey, then a blue disc appears from 2.58 s with spring 1 − e^(−6.5t)·cos(15t).
- Press: the button shrinks by up to 20% at 2.96–3.21 s (half sine). At 3.13–3.41 s the text moves 70 px up while fading out.
- The cursor returns to the start once the text is half faded (about 3.27 s); at 3.51–3.81 s the blue fades.
When to use it: Use it to show someone typing: a prompt, a search query, a chat message.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/006.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/motion.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

· 造型：中性灰白几何体（哑光 #e8e8e8），无贴图、无光泽、无反射、无金属感，无任何风格化笔触；轮廓用 1px 浅灰描边（#b4b4b4）保持可读性。
· 阴影：单层柔和接触阴影（不透明度约 0.12），仅用于指示物体与地面的关系，不参与造型塑造。
· 背景：纯白或单一浅灰平涂，不加渐变、不加纹理、不加氛围粒子。
· 唯一继承项是运动学（时序、缓动、幅度），外观全部替换为中性材质。
· 缓动：On the ground (first and last 10% of each bounce): vertical scale goes between 0.52 (moment of impact) and 1.28 (moment of leaving) on a quadratic curve.
· 幅度：A round character, radius 37. One bounce per 1.175 s (four per 4.7 s), a 92 px parabola. It drifts ±150 px sideways on a sine wave over the cycle. In the air: vertical scale = 1 + 0.28 × s^3, where s is the time offset from the apex (0 at the apex, 1 at take-off and touchdown), so it is stretched where it moves fast. Horizontal scale is always 1 ÷ vertical (volume is preserved). The transform is anchored at the feet. The shadow gets smaller and thinner with height. Short yellow lines flick out left and right at each landing (for about 18% of a bounce).
· 可替换槽位：{主体形状} / {材质} / {主色} / {背景} / {投影} / {文字} —— 先在此白模版上验证节奏，确认后再套具体风格的配色、材质与质感。

Please use "Shape morph" (モーフィング), one of the names in "Motion graphics moves".
Motion Prompt #012

What it is: One shape turns smoothly into another
What the sample shows: A shape changes smoothly from circle to square to star to heart, with its colour.
Spec:
- Four shapes, 1.175 s each: circle → square with rounded-off corners → star → heart → back to circle. Base radius 64.
- Each segment holds first, then morphs to the next shape between 0.62 s and 0.04 s before its end (0.58 s).
- Every outline is stored as 240 points; points with the same index are linearly interpolated. Progress uses backOut (s = 1.6), so it overshoots slightly.
- Colour: blue → coral → yellow → mint, blended with quadratic ease-in-out.
- During the morph the scale swells by 1 + 0.07 × sin(π × progress).
- Four dots below; the dot for the current shape is larger and coloured.
When to use it: Use it to turn one icon or logo into another without a cut.

· 造型：中性灰白几何体（哑光 #e8e8e8），无贴图、无光泽、无反射、无金属感，无任何风格化笔触；轮廓用 1px 浅灰描边（#b4b4b4）保持可读性。
· 阴影：单层柔和接触阴影（不透明度约 0.12），仅用于指示物体与地面的关系，不参与造型塑造。
· 背景：纯白或单一浅灰平涂，不加渐变、不加纹理、不加氛围粒子。
· 唯一继承项是运动学（时序、缓动、幅度），外观全部替换为中性材质。
· 时序：Subject: a person stands still 8 m ahead; the final size matches 03 Dolly in (about 3.6×) Top-right readout shows the focal length in mm (24mm → 87mm)
· 缓动：Exponential interpolation: f = 330 × (8/2.2)^p, where p is a cubic ease-in-out from 0.5 s to 3.4 s (2.9 s) Return: hold 3.4–4.2 s, then cross-fade back to the start over the last 0.5 s (one pass = 4.7 s)
· 幅度：Camera: position and direction fixed (height 1.5 m); only the focal length changes, 330 px → 1200 px (shown as 24mm → 87mm, about 3.6×) No parallax: the foreground post and rock, the person, buildings and mountains all scale by the same ratio (overlaps do not change)
· 可替换槽位：{主体形状} / {材质} / {主色} / {背景} / {投影} / {文字} —— 先在此白模版上验证节奏，确认后再套具体风格的配色、材质与质感。

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Tracking shot" (トラッキング), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #029

What it is: Move along with the subject
What the sample shows: The camera moves sideways at the same speed as a walking person; the person stays centred while nearer posts sweep past faster.
Spec:
- Camera: moves right at a constant 1.7 m/s (x = -4.0 m → +4.0 m in 4.7 s); height 1.3 m, facing straight ahead; no easing
- Subject: a person walks at the same x as the camera (7.5 m away) and stays in the centre of frame; legs and arms swing by sin(u×7)×0.42 rad
- Parallax: posts every 1.6 m at 4 m depth sweep left fastest, then trees, then buildings (48 m away); mountains hardly move
- Top-right readout shows "→ 1.7m/s"
- Repeat: jumps back to the start every 4.7 s (posts and ground grid line up at the seam; background buildings and trees jump)
When to use it: To follow a walking or running subject and keep the sense of movement while showing their action.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/029.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/camera.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

Please use "Orbit (Arc shot)" (オービット), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #030

What it is: Circle around the subject
What the sample shows: The camera travels on a circle around the subject; the person stays centred while the trees and buildings behind sweep sideways.
Spec:
- Camera: travels on a circle of radius 6 m centred on the person (9 m ahead), from -0.95 rad → +0.95 rad (-54° → +54°, about 109° in total)
- Direction: always faces the centre (yaw = -angle); height 1.7 m, pitch fixed at -0.07 rad (about 4° down)
- Timing: 0.5 s to 3.6 s (3.1 s), cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1))
- Subject: the person does not move; a white dot on the face shifts sideways with the angle; a dashed circle of radius 1.3 m marks the ground
- Background: 12 trees evenly spaced on a 10 m radius cross behind the person as the camera moves round
- Return: hold 3.6–4.2 s, then cross-fade back over the last 0.5 s; top-right readout shows the angle (-54° → +54°)
When to use it: To show a person or product in three dimensions, or to emphasise an entrance or a key moment.

- Top-right readout shows the height (↑ 1.4m → ↑ 9.0m)
When to use it: To pull away from a person at the end of a scene or to reveal how large the location is.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Dolly zoom (Vertigo)" (ドリーズーム), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #032

What it is: Subject stays, background warps
What the sample shows: The camera pulls back while zooming in by the same ratio; the person keeps the same size and only the background closes in.
Spec:
- Camera: distance d to the person (8 m ahead) widens from 3.2 m → 8 m (a 4.8 m pull-back); height 1.3 m
- Focal length: f = 330 × d/8 px, i.e. 132 px → 330 px (shown as 10mm → 24mm), keeping distance ÷ focal length constant
- Timing: 0.5 s to 3.4 s (2.9 s), cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1))
- Subject: the person does not move and keeps the same height in frame; blue dashed lines 160 px wide at head (1.8 m) and feet show the size is constant
- Background: buildings (48 m away) grow about 2.2× and mountains about 2.4×, closing in behind the person, while the ground in front of the person shrinks
- Return: hold 3.4–4.2 s, then cross-fade back to the start over the last 0.5 s (one pass = 4.7 s)
When to use it: For a moment of realisation, or to show unease or shock visually.

- Return: hold 2.6–4.2 s, then cross-fade back over the last 0.5 s; top-right readout shows focus distance (◎ 2m → ◎ 9m)

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Handheld" (手持ち), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #034

What it is: A slight shake, as if the camera were held by hand
What the sample shows: Adds a small, irregular shake to the whole frame, as if the camera were held by hand instead of on a tripod.
Spec:
- Camera: position almost fixed; yaw, pitch, roll and height each get a sum of sine waves with different periods (T = 2π×u/4.7)
- Yaw (rad) = 0.016·sin(3T) + 0.008·sin(7T+1) + 0.004·sin(13T+2), at most about ±1.6°
- Pitch (rad) = 0.012·sin(4T+2) + 0.006·sin(9T+0.5) + 0.003·sin(17T+1.2), at most about ±1.2°
- Roll (rad) = 0.02·sin(5T+1) + 0.008·sin(11T+3), at most about ±1.6°; height = 1.5 + 0.03·sin(6T) m
- Subject: a person stands still 6.5 m ahead; the shake runs continuously with no easing or hold
- All multipliers are integers, so it loops seamlessly every 4.7 s; top-right readout shows "HANDHELD"
When to use it: To give a documentary feel or the sense of being present in the scene.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/034.txt

items.promptRaw:
Please use "FPV drone shot" (FPV), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #035

What it is: Fast, immersive fly-through
What the sample shows: A first-person view flying low and fast between two rows of trees, banking from side to side.
Spec:
- Camera: flies forward at a constant 14 m/s (shown as 50km/h) with no easing; pitch fixed at -0.05 rad
- Weave (T = 2π×u/4.7, two swings per 4.7 s): sideways 0.6·sin(2T-0.4) m, height 1.4 + 0.5·sin(2T) m
- Bank: roll 0.22·sin(2T+0.6) rad (about ±12.6°), yaw 0.05·sin(2T) rad (about ±2.9°)
- No subject. Trees 4.2 m tall stand 3.6 m to each side, every 8 m, the two rows offset by 4 m, and rush toward the camera
- Speed lines: 10 radial strokes about 32–76 px long (longer toward the sides) in translucent grey, flowing outward and recycling
- No hold and no cross-fade reset (the tree rows shift phase when it restarts every 4.7 s)
When to use it: For speed and immersion, or to fly through a location in one continuous move.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/035.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/camera.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Wipe" (ワイプ), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #045

What it is: A moving edge replaces the shot
What the sample shows: A vertical edge moves from left to right and the next picture replaces the current one behind it.
Spec:
- Join: 1.1 s, from 1.7 s to 2.8 s; the edge travels from just outside the left side (x = -4 px) to just outside the right side (x = 543 px)
- Easing: cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1))
- The incoming picture shows left of the edge and the outgoing one right of it; neither picture moves (a reveal by clipping, not a push)
- Edge: a 4 px blue vertical line, visible only while it is moving
- Camera: fixed in both pictures; the subjects do not move either
- Alternates A→B and B→A every 4.7 s (9.4 s for the round trip); top-right readout shows "A → B" / "B → A"
When to use it: To mark a clear change of scene or topic, or to switch between the two sides of a comparison.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/045.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/camera.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Smash cut" (スマッシュカット), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #046

What it is: Abrupt cut to a contrasting scene
What the sample shows: A quiet scene of a person asleep cuts with no warning straight to an intense one; the volume meter jumps at the same moment.
Spec:
- Join: a straight cut at 2.4 s (0 frames); no transition effect, the contrast does the work
- Outgoing shot (0–2.4 s): fixed camera (height 1.2 m, focal length 330 px); a person lying down 7 m away, three "z" letters float up and fade; volume meter at about 0–1 of 8 bars (0.08±0.04)
- Incoming shot (2.4–4.2 s): focal length 2.6× (858 px) for a tight framing, rolled -0.12 rad (about -7°); the person has both arms raised, with 18 radial blue lines
- Shake in the incoming shot: roll ±0.03 rad (about 6 cycles per second) and yaw ±0.006 rad (about 8 per second); volume meter at 0.85±0.15, nearly full
- Return: cross-fade back to the quiet shot over the last 0.5 s (quadratic ease-in-out)
- Top-right readout shows "♪ 静か" (quiet) → "♪ 大音量" (loud)
When to use it: For comedy or shock, showing in an instant the gap between calm and chaos or between expectation and reality.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/046.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/camera.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

Please use "J-cut" (Jカット), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #047

What it is: Next scene's audio starts first
What the sample shows: The next scene's audio starts before the picture changes; the picture is shown on top with video and audio timelines below.
Spec:
- Join: the picture is a straight cut; only the audio switches to the next scene (B) before the picture does. The offset is 20% of the timeline (0.72 s)
- Playhead: moves left to right at constant speed over 3.6 s (0.4 s to 4.0 s); audio switches at 35% (about 1.66 s), picture at 55% (about 2.38 s)
- In the offset section (35–55%) the picture is still A while the audio is already B; the section is marked with a pale blue band and two blue dashed lines
- Layout: the top 134 px is the picture (fixed camera, subjects do not move); the bottom 74 px holds two timeline rows, video and audio (A grey, B pale blue, waveform on the audio row)
- Labels: "映像A / 映像B" (video A / B) at bottom left of the picture; the audio now playing at bottom right ("♪ Aの音" grey → "♪ Bの音" blue)
- Return: cross-fade back to the start over the last 0.5 s (one pass = 4.7 s)
When to use it: To build anticipation for the next scene, or to make a change of scene or speaker feel natural.

Please use "L-cut" (Lカット), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions".
Motion Prompt #048

What it is: Previous scene's audio carries over
What the sample shows: The previous scene's audio carries on for a while after the picture has changed; the picture is shown on top with video and audio timelines below.
Spec:
- Join: the picture is a straight cut; only the audio switches to the next scene (B) after the picture does. The offset is 20% of the timeline (0.72 s)

- In the offset section (55–75%) the picture is already B while the audio is still A; the section is marked with a pale blue band and two blue dashed lines

- Labels: "映像A / 映像B" (video A / B) at bottom left of the picture; the audio now playing at bottom right ("♪ Aの音" grey → "♪ Bの音" blue)
- Return: cross-fade back to the start over the last 0.5 s (one pass = 4.7 s)
When to use it: To keep a speaker's voice running while showing the listener's reaction or related footage.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Tabs" (タブ), one of the names in "UI component names".
Motion Prompt #057

What it is: Click a label to switch which panel is shown
What the sample shows: Clicking the tabs "Overview, Pricing, Reviews" in turn slides a blue underline across and swaps the content below.
Spec:
- 4.5 s cycle on a 542×191 card. Three tabs at x 24, 114, 204, widths 70, 70, 100; a 2 px divider at y 50 and a 4 px blue underline.
- The cursor clicks the second tab at 1.0 s, the third at 2.2 s and the first at 3.4 s.
- Underline: position and width move to the new tab over 0.25 s from each click with easeInOutCubic (from the third back to the first it passes through the middle).
- Labels: selected is blue and bold, others grey; the switch happens at 1.1, 2.3 and 3.5 s.
- Content: the old panel fades out linearly in 0.2 s; 0.1 s later the new one fades in over 0.2 s while rising 8 px.
When to use it: Use it to show several related views in the same space and let people switch between them.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/057.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/ui.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Preloader" (ローディング画面), one of the names in "Landing page & web effects".
Motion Prompt #089

What it is: A screen shown while the page loads
What the sample shows: On a navy screen the number under the logo counts from 0% to 100%; then the screen lifts away and the page underneath fades in.
Spec:
- A navy screen fills the viewport with a logo, a number (28 px) and a bar (180 × 4).
- 0→100% at 0.25–2.1 s (cubic ease-out, rounded to whole numbers); the bar fills in orange at the same rate.
- At 2.3–2.85 s the whole screen moves up 168 px and out (cubic ease-in-out).
- The page heading and photo fade in 0→1 and rise from 14 px below at 2.35–2.95 s (cubic ease-out).
- At 4.25–4.75 s the screen comes back down from the top, at 0% (the next load).
When to use it: Use it on image- or video-heavy sites to turn the loading wait into a brand moment.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/089.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/lp.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

Please use "Infinite scroll" (無限スクロール), one of the names in "Landing page & web effects".
Motion Prompt #091

What it is: More items load automatically at the bottom
What the sample shows: Scrolling down to the end of the list brings up a spinner, then three new items are added so reading can go on.

- Each cycle advances by three items (156 px). The content repeats every three items, so the end of the cycle looks the same as the start.
When to use it: Use it for feeds and news lists that people should keep reading without paging.

Please use "Page transition" (ページ遷移アニメーション), one of the names in "Landing page & web effects".

What it is: An animation that bridges two pages
What the sample shows: Clicking a card in the work list sweeps an orange panel across from the left; the URL changes and the panel exits to the right on the detail page. "Back to list" returns the same way.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Butterfly lighting" (バタフライライティング), one of the names in "Photo looks, lighting & styles".
Motion Prompt #102

What it is: High frontal light that casts a butterfly shadow under the nose
What the sample shows: A light in front of the face and high above comes on; the face lights evenly on both sides and only a small symmetrical shadow falls under the chin.
Spec:
- Scene 1: a head-and-shoulders figure in front of a horizon at y 150 (head centre x 270, y 78, radius 29 px, no face or hair). the background drops to a darker scene (sky #E7E5E1)
- Head: entirely lit #FFC75A (no shadow side)
- Shadow under the chin: an ellipse centred at y 78+1.06R, 0.72R wide and 0.38R tall (R = 29, about 21×11 px), colour #33405A
- Body: lit within ±0.8×56 px of the centre, thin outer strips keep the base colour; plan shows the light on the camera side (0°), top-right readout "0° · ↑45°"
- Timing: the effect comes in from 0.4 s to 1.4 s, holds until 4.0 s and is gone again by 4.8 s (one pass = 5 s, cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)))
When to use it: For beauty and fashion portraits that flatter the face.

Please use "Panning shot" (流し撮り), one of the names in "Photo looks, lighting & styles".
Motion Prompt #108

What it is: Follow a moving subject so only the background streaks
What the sample shows: The camera follows the moving car: the car stays sharp in the middle of the frame while only the buildings, trees and lamps behind it streak sideways.
Spec:
- Street corner: buildings, trees and lamps behind a road at y 132–162 (no large person in front)

- Both springs are precomputed in 1/600 s steps; drawing only looks values up.
- In the last 0.3 s of each move the swing is faded to 0 with smoothstep, so the loop has no seam.

items.meaning: 沿设定的曲线移动
items.description: A paper plane follows a dotted path, turning as it goes and looping the loop on the way.
items.ask: 让纸飞机沿这条曲线的运动路径在 4 s 内飞完，机头始终朝向前进方向。
items.timing: One pass per 4.7 s, from off-screen left to off-screen right. The path is x = 270 + 112θ − 150·sinθ, y = 106 − 74·cosθ for θ = −π→π, which makes a loop at the top centre. θ advances in proportion to time (so the speed along the path is not constant; the loop looks slower). - Top-right readout shows the height (↕ 1.0m → ↕ 3.2m)
When to use it: To show a shelf or a building from bottom to top smoothly, or to change the eye level without tilting.

Please use "Hyperlapse" (ハイパーラプス), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions, part 2".
Motion Prompt #171

What it is: A time-lapse shot while the camera travels
What the sample shows: The camera travels forward along a street while the sun, clouds and passers-by run in fast forward: a time-lapse that moves.
Spec:
- Camera: moves forward 0 m → 22 m (height 1.6 m, pitch +0.05 rad) while the sun, clouds and figures fast-forward through 12 hours (#039 Time-lapse keeps the camera still)
- Timing: 0.4 s to 4.1 s (3.7 s), cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1))
- Street: 12 buildings at x = ±7.5 m (5–55 m deep, 8–16 m tall) approach the camera and leave the frame

- Building shadows fall away from the sun and swing as it moves (translucent grey); the mountains move with the camera so they keep their size
- Return: cross-fade back to the start over the last 0.5 s; top-right readout shows the clock and the distance travelled (06:00 · 0m → 18:00 · 22m)
When to use it: To cover a long distance and a long stretch of time in one sweep through a city or a building.

· 造型：中性灰白几何体（哑光 #e8e8e8），无贴图、无光泽、无反射、无金属感，无任何风格化笔触；轮廓用 1px 浅灰描边（#b4b4b4）保持可读性。

· 唯一继承项是运动学（时序、缓动、幅度），外观全部替换为中性材质。
· 时序：Subject: a person walks 5 m ahead of the camera at the same speed; legs and arms take 5 strides per 4.7 s 8 m is a multiple of the grid (2 m) and tree (8 m) spacing, so it loops seamlessly every 4.7 s; top-right readout shows "STEADICAM" Trees: 3.6 m tall at x = -5 m and 3.2 m tall at x = +5 m, every 8 m (the two rows offset by 4 m); the mountains and sun move with the camera

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Follow shot" (フォローショット), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions, part 2".
Motion Prompt #174

What it is: Follow behind the subject as they move
What the sample shows: The camera trails a weaving walker along the same path a few metres behind; the person stays near the centre, seen from the back.
Spec:
- Path: the person walks the curve x = 1.8·sin(2.2s), depth z = 4 + 9s (s from 0 to 1), from 4 m to 13 m away
- Camera: follows on the same curve at s-0.4 (about 3.6–3.9 m behind) and always faces the person, yaw = atan2(person x - camera x, person z - camera z); height 1.5 m
- Timing: 0.3 s to 4.2 s (3.9 s), cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)); legs and arms swing by sin(s×30)×0.42 rad
- The person stays near the centre of frame, seen from behind; posts and a rock beside the path sweep past in the foreground (#029 Tracking shot runs alongside)
- Return: cross-fade back to the start over the last 0.5 s (one pass = 4.7 s); top-right readout shows the distance to the person (FOLLOW 3.6–3.9m)
When to use it: To enter a place together with a character, or for a third-person, game-like view.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/174.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/camera2.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Locked-off shot" (ロックオフ), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions, part 2".
Motion Prompt #175

What it is: Camera fixed; only the subject moves
What the sample shows: A person crosses in front of a tripod-fixed camera and a car passes behind; the camera does not move by a pixel.
Spec:
- Camera: completely fixed (height 1.4 m, facing forward, focal length 330 px); only the subjects move
- Subject: a person crosses left to right at constant speed 6.5 m ahead (x = -6.2 m → +6.2 m in 4.7 s); legs and arms swing by sin(u×7)×0.42 rad
- A grey car crosses right to left 15 m away (x = +16 m → -16 m in 4.7 s)
- Both start and end outside the frame, so it loops seamlessly every 4.7 s
- A grey tripod mark at bottom left; top-right readout shows "LOCKED" (#040 Freeze frame stops the footage time; here time runs and only the camera is still)
When to use it: To make the subject stand out by contrast, for fixed-point observation, or as a base for time-lapse and compositing.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/175.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/camera2.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

Please use "Fly-through" (フライスルー), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions, part 2".
Motion Prompt #176

What it is: Fly through an opening into the next space
What the sample shows: The camera flies toward a wall with a window, passes through the opening and comes out into the place beyond.
Spec:
- Camera: moves forward 0 m → 12.5 m (height 1.3 m, direction fixed); a wall with a window stands 8 m ahead and the camera passes through it
- Timing: 0.5 s to 3.6 s (3.1 s), cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1))
- Wall: a pale grey plane 80 m wide and 14 m tall with a window 2.4 m wide and 2.2 m tall (sill at 0.15 m); through it a person (0.3 m right, 14.5 m away), trees, buildings and mountains are visible
- Pass-through: the wall stops being drawn 0.25 m in front of the camera; by then the window edge is outside the frame (half-width about 1580 px), so it vanishes unseen
- After the pass the place beyond fills the frame and the camera closes to 2 m from the person (#035 FPV drone shot keeps weaving between trees)
- Return: hold 3.6–4.2 s, then cross-fade back to the start over the last 0.5 s; top-right readout shows the distance to the window ("窓まで 8.0m" → "通過", passed)
When to use it: To enter a building as an opening move, or to travel from one place to another in a single move.

· 造型：中性灰白几何体（哑光 #e8e8e8），无贴图、无光泽、无反射、无金属感，无任何风格化笔触；轮廓用 1px 浅灰描边（#b4b4b4）保持可读性。
· 阴影：单层柔和接触阴影（不透明度约 0.12），仅用于指示物体与地面的关系，不参与造型塑造。
· 背景：纯白或单一浅灰平涂，不加渐变、不加纹理、不加氛围粒子。
· 唯一继承项是运动学（时序、缓动、幅度），外观全部替换为中性材质。
· 时序：Wall: a pale grey plane 80 m wide and 14 m tall with a window 2.4 m wide and 2.2 m tall (sill at 0.15 m); through it a person (0.3 m right, 14.5 m away), trees, buildings and mountains are visible
· 缓动：Timing: 0.5 s to 3.6 s (3.1 s), cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1)) After the pass the place beyond fills the frame and the camera closes to 2 m from the person (#035 FPV drone shot keeps weaving between trees) Return: hold 3.6–4.2 s, then cross-fade back to the start over the last 0.5 s; top-right readout shows the distance to the window ("窓まで 8.0m" → "通過", passed)
· 幅度：Camera: moves forward 0 m → 12.5 m (height 1.3 m, direction fixed); a wall with a window stands 8 m ahead and the camera passes through it Pass-through: the wall stops being drawn 0.25 m in front of the camera; by then the window edge is outside the frame (half-width about 1580 px), so it vanishes unseen
· 可替换槽位：{主体形状} / {材质} / {主色} / {背景} / {投影} / {文字} —— 先在此白模版上验证节奏，确认后再套具体风格的配色、材质与质感。

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Low angle" (ローアングル), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions, part 2".
Motion Prompt #177

What it is: Shoot from low down, looking up
What the sample shows: The camera drops to near the ground and looks up; the person looks big and the buildings tower.
Spec:
- Camera: lowers from 1.5 m to 0.35 m while the pitch goes 0 → +0.32 rad (about 18° up); no movement forward or back
- Timing: 0.6 s to 2.2 s (1.6 s), cubic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1))
- Subject: a person stands still 4.5 m ahead; an 11.8 m tower stands 3 m left, 22 m away. As the camera looks up, person and tower stretch upward and the horizon drops
- Hold: stays at the low angle from 2.2 s to 4.2 s (time to read the composition itself)
- Return: cross-fade back to eye level over the last 0.5 s (one pass = 4.7 s); top-right readout shows angle and height (↗ 0° · 1.5m → ↗ 18° · 0.4m)
When to use it: To make a person look powerful or large, or to emphasise the height of a building.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/177.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/camera2.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

· 造型：中性灰白几何体（哑光 #e8e8e8），无贴图、无光泽、无反射、无金属感，无任何风格化笔触；轮廓用 1px 浅灰描边（#b4b4b4）保持可读性。
· 阴影：单层柔和接触阴影（不透明度约 0.12），仅用于指示物体与地面的关系，不参与造型塑造。
· 背景：纯白或单一浅灰平涂，不加渐变、不加纹理、不加氛围粒子。
· 唯一继承项是运动学（时序、缓动、幅度），外观全部替换为中性材质。
· 时序：Bottom strip: three sections A (grey), detail (blue), A (grey) with a playhead; what is cut in belongs to the same scene (21 Cutaway shows a different subject)
· 缓动：Join: two straight cuts (0 frames); to the detail at 1.6 s and back to the scene at 2.9 s (the detail lasts 1.3 s) Top-right readout shows "SHOT A" → "INSERT" → "SHOT A"; at 4.7 s it cuts straight back to the start
· 幅度：Main shot (A): fixed camera (height 1.4 m); a person stands 0.6 m left, 6 m away, with a watch (dark dot) on the wrist; a post 2.2 m right, 4 m away Detail (INSERT): a big close-up of the wrist from the same scene; a blue sleeve (600×92 px, rotated -0.35 rad) on pale blue, a white dial (radius 58 px), dark hands and a blue second hand that makes one turn in 1.3 s
· 可替换槽位：{主体形状} / {材质} / {主色} / {背景} / {投影} / {文字} —— 先在此白模版上验证节奏，确认后再套具体风格的配色、材质与质感。

items.promptRaw:
Please use "Morph cut" (モーフカット), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions, part 2".
Motion Prompt #186

What it is: Blend two takes so the join disappears
What the sample shows: Two takes of the same person are joined by smoothly interpolating position and pose, so nothing jumps as in a jump cut.
Spec:
- Take 1 (0–2.0 s): fixed camera (height 1.45 m); the person stands 0.4 m left, 3.3 m away, arms and legs at -0.45 rad. Take 2 (from 2.45 s): 0.35 m right, +0.55 rad. Both sway slightly by 0.12·sin(t×3) rad
- Morph (2.0–2.45 s, 0.45 s): the position is interpolated with a quadratic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1)), and the two poses are drawn at the same interpolated position and cross-faded
- Only during the morph a blur of sin(q×π)×2.2 px is applied to the whole frame to soften the join (#041 Jump cut lets the position jump)
- Bottom strip: take 1 (grey), morph (blue, narrow), take 2 (grey) with a playhead
- Return: cross-fade back to the start of take 1 over the last 0.5 s; top-right readout shows "TAKE 1" → "MORPH" → "TAKE 2"
When to use it: To tighten an interview or narration, or to remove a slip without drawing attention.

Reference implementation (Canvas 2D, a function whose picture depends only on the time): https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/en/e/186.txt
Shared helper code: https://showheyohtaki.github.io/motion-prompt/api/v1/kit/camera2.js
Keep the shapes, timing and easing values of the reference implementation as they are, and change only the text, colours and assets to fit what I am making.

Please use "Fade to black" (フェードアウト), one of the names in "Camera moves & transitions, part 2".
Motion Prompt #187

What it is: The picture darkens to black
What the sample shows: The whole picture sinks to black, and the next scene brightens out of the black.
Spec:
- Fade out: from 1.4 s to 2.6 s (1.2 s) black (rgb(20,20,24)) is laid over the outgoing picture with opacity 0 → 100%, quadratic ease-in-out (about cubic-bezier(0.45,0,0.55,1))
- Black: fully black from 2.6 s to 3.1 s; at 2.9 s the incoming picture is swapped in unseen, with a straight cut
- Fade in: from 3.1 s to 4.3 s (1.2 s) the black goes from 100% → 0 with the same easing
- Camera: fixed in both pictures (A at height 1.4 m; B at height 1.6 m, pitch +0.1 rad); the subjects do not move either
- Alternates A→B and B→A every 4.7 s (9.4 s for the round trip); top-right readout shows "FADE OUT" / "FADE IN"; the viewfinder marks stay over the black
When to use it: For a chapter break, a long passage of time, or the end of a story.
